title: Ultimatum security findings
description: Shape of .ultimatum/security/findings.json. Enforced by `ult findings validate` (scripts/ultlib/findings.py); that validator is the contract and additionally rejects duplicate ids/fingerprints, found_by == verified_by, unsafe paths, and any value that redact() would change (an unredacted secret). Unknown fields are allowed but reported as warnings.

scope.description: What was reviewed: target, ref, environment, constraints.

source_ref.description: git ref reviewed, with a note if the tree was dirty

tools.description: Tools that ran / did not run, from `ult scan` output.

authorization.description: What the user authorized (read-only by default).

id.description: F-001 style; auto-assigned by `ult findings add`.

file.description: Repo-relative path: no leading '/', no '..', no control characters.

endpoint.description: Route, CLI command, job, or message handler, e.g. 'GET /docs/{id}'.

actor.description: Who attacks and what they start with (e.g. 'any logged-in user of tenant A').

boundary.description: The rule that should hold and fails, e.g. 'users read only their own account's documents'.

preconditions.description: Role, config, flag, timing; 'none beyond a normal account' is a valid value.

impact.description: What was shown: which data/actions, whose.

evidence.description: file:line quotes, commands with exit codes, test names. Include the strongest control that was checked.

missing_evidence.description: needs-validation only: the exact fact that would settle it.

rejection_reason.description: rejected only: the control or fact that refutes the claim.
